draft.title: Blue-coverage percent + accent-hue count sweep
draft.principle_summary: Two independent, checkable claims justify computing the blue-restraint rule instead of eyeballing it. First, Feature Integration Theory (Treisman and Gelade 1980, T1, foundational and heavily replicated) shows a unique-color singleton is detected via fast pre-attentive pop-out with reaction time flat against distractor count, but only while the target stays rare and unique in the field; once a color repeats densely or a second novel hue appears, the pop-out advantage degrades because the target is no longer a unique feature. This is the actual mechanism behind blue disappearing into the prose and behind demoting the weakest of three or more vertically aligned blues. Second, WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (T1, formal W3C AA standard) independently requires every UI component and its states to hold 3 to 1 contrast against adjacent colors, a constraint orthogonal to sparsity: a sparse blue link can still fail contrast, and a compliant-contrast blue can still be visually over-dense. Both checks must run, they answer different questions. Third, the existing three-blue-strings figure has no traceable empirical source; it patterns like the 60-30-10 color-scheme rule, an undated design-folklore convention with no controlled study located (CONV), not a measured threshold, so it must be relabeled honestly rather than left looking researched.
draft.solen_current: LOCKFILE.md lines 158-160: "Squint test (per screen): zoom out, blue must disappear into the prose. Soft ceiling ~3 blue strings per viewport on content screens, 0-1 on forms/full-page states. If one blue string repeats inside the same component, or 3+ blues line up vertically (blue staircase), demote the weakest to ink." Lines 162-176 give a per-surface blue/ink verdict table (review counts, Mehr lesen, Passwort vergessen, Andern jump-links = blue; See-all, Skip, secondary buttons, feature-row icon tints = ink). Line 178-180 GUARDRAIL: blue stays off non-interactive text and button-geometry elements; "Drift A9 flags blue on non-interactive text + blue-filled primaries; the squint test catches the rest" (i.e. the squint test itself is explicitly acknowledged as the un-mechanized half). LOCKFILE section 1 rule 4 (line 18): "No new semantic hues invented... Don't pick a nice teal for a status" - also prose-only, no hue-count check exists. RATIONALE.md section 28 (gap register, lines 819-850) already names this: D2 "Blue-coverage percent + accent-hue count per rendered screen (the most-relitigated rule, measurable as pixels), Mechanizable: YES" and calls it "the most-complained axis" alongside D1, second in the recommended build order after D4.
draft.gap: The ~3-blue-strings ceiling and the "no new hues" rule are both bare assertions: no formula, no script, no threshold source. RATIONALE.md itself flags D2 as open and unbuilt (section 28). Drift A9 only catches two binary violations (blue on non-interactive text, blue-filled primary CTA); it has no counting, no clustering, and no vertical-alignment check, so the actual soft-ceiling rule ("~3 strings", "3+ blues in a column", "one string repeats in a component") still requires a human to zoom out and squint every single time, which is exactly the condition RATIONALE.md's own gap register calls "the exact condition the house ledger says degrades advice into noise" (line 821). There is also no pixel-level check at all, so a single oversized blue-filled shape (technically one DOM element, therefore one "string") could pass the string count while visually dominating the screen; and no hue-count check exists to catch an invented semantic color creeping in alongside the closed LOCKFILE palette.
draft.proposed_addition:
COMPUTABLE METRIC SPEC for RATIONALE.md domain 28 / D2 (build-ready description, no code written).

INPUTS (per rendered screen, captured at the two standard verification viewports already used elsewhere in this repo, 375x812 mobile and 1440x900 desktop, plus a "forms/full-page-state" flag set by the caller since that class carries a stricter ceiling per the existing rule):
- The live DOM within the viewport's visible bounding box (scrollY = 0 unless the caller passes a scroll offset for a specific fold).
- A rendered screenshot of the same bounding box.
- The closed LOCKFILE token palette: s-accent.DEFAULT #276EF1, s-accent.deep #1E54B7, s-success #16A34A, s-error (red), s-warning.text #B45309, star #FFC32B, save-heart #FF3366, s-surcharge #EA580C, s-urgency #C2410C, s-ink family, neutrals.

METRIC 1, blue-string count (mechanizes the existing squint test exactly):
- For every visible text-bearing element (has a non-empty text node child, not display:none/visibility:hidden/opacity:0), read computed color, border-color, and background-color.
- Classify as a "blue string" if color or border-color is within RGB distance <= 10 (or CIEDE2000 <= 4) of s-accent.DEFAULT or s-accent.deep.
- Exclude the LOCKED system-state exceptions named in LOCKFILE lines 175-176 (focus-visible ring, Spinner arc, form-input focus halo, stepper discs, walk-in LIVE pill) since those are frozen literals, not squint-test subjects.
- Count distinct qualifying elements = S_blue.
- Flag any qualifying element whose background-color ALSO matches s-accent (a blue fill, not blue text) as a separate HARD violation of the "primary CTA never blue-filled" rule (LOCKFILE line 16), independent of the count.
- Flag if two qualifying elements share the same nearest ancestor component boundary (same card/row container) as "repeats inside one component" (existing rule, line 159).
- Flag "blue staircase" if 3 or more qualifying elements have bounding-box horizontal centers within +/-20px of each other (a vertical column, existing rule, line 160); when flagged, name the weakest candidate to demote by lowest computed font-size, then lowest information value.
- Threshold: content screens S_blue <= 3 = PASS, 4 = WARN, 5+ = FLAG. Forms/full-page-state screens S_blue <= 1 = PASS, 2 = WARN, 3+ = FLAG. State plainly in the tool's output that this numeric ceiling is CONV (unsourced convention, patterns like 60-30-10), not a T1/T2 finding, so a future Taste Lab round can recalibrate it without pretending a study is being overturned.

METRIC 2, blue pixel-coverage percent (catches what a per-element count misses: one oversized filled shape):
- From the screenshot, classify every pixel by nearest LOCKFILE token using CIEDE2000 distance, floor threshold 10.
- P_blue = (pixels classified as s-accent.DEFAULT or .deep) divided by (total viewport pixels), times 100.
- Threshold, DERIVED not independently studied (label T3): cap P_blue at 3% on content screens, 1% on forms, chosen to sit inside the 80% neutral-surface / 17% ink budget CLAUDE.md rule 3 already asserts, with blue explicitly the sparse remainder. Flag if exceeded even when S_blue is within budget; this is the specific case that catches an oversized single accent shape.

METRIC 3, distinct accent-hue count (mechanizes LOCKFILE section 1 rule 4, "no new semantic hues invented"):
- Cluster all non-neutral pixels (exclude anything within CIEDE2000 <= 6 of white #FFFFFF, sunken #F4F4F5, ink #0A0A0A, or the grey family, and exclude photography regions if a bounding box for imagery is supplied) into 15-degree HSL hue bins.
- Keep only clusters whose area exceeds 0.3% of the viewport (filters anti-aliasing and compression noise).
- Map each surviving cluster to its nearest closed LOCKFILE semantic token (deltaE <= 15). Any cluster that does not map to one of the seven-to-eight enumerated tokens is flagged INVENTED HUE, a hard fail against the existing prose rule.
- Report the count of distinct semantic tokens actually present on screen (H_accent) as an informational number; more than 4-5 co-occurring on one screen is a softer richness/restraint flag, explicitly logged as CONV/needs-calibration (not asserted here as a hard ceiling), a candidate Taste Lab probe rather than a shipped threshold.

BOUNDARY: this spec measures presence and count, not the separate WCAG 1.4.11 requirement that every qualifying blue UI component independently clear 3:1 contrast against its adjacent background; that is a distinct, already-standard check (T1, W3C) that should run alongside this one, not be folded into it, since a screen can pass one and fail the other. Also state explicitly in the RATIONALE.md entry that Metric 1's numeric ceiling (3 / 0-1) is CONV, carried forward from the existing prose rule rather than newly derived, so nobody downstream mistakes "mechanized" for "empirically validated."
draft.taste_lab_probe: Not required to ship the metric (D2 is diagnostic, not generative), but flagged for later calibration: once the script exists, run it against 8-10 already-shipped, owner-approved screens (the ones LOCKFILE cites as reference, e.g. the booking wizard, checkout summary, search results) to see what S_blue and P_blue actually measure on surfaces nobody has complained about. If the approved set clusters at 2-4 rather than exactly 3, and forms cluster at 0-1 as stated, that is weak converging evidence the CONV number is at least locally consistent; if it scatters widely, the ceiling needs an explicit Taste Lab round rather than staying asserted.

sources.claim: A unique-feature (e.g. a singleton color) target is detected via fast, parallel pre-attentive processing with reaction time roughly flat against distractor count; this pop-out effect depends on the target remaining a rare, unique feature in the visual field, which is the mechanism behind why a sparse accent color reads instantly and a dense or repeated one does not
sources.source: Treisman, A. and Gelade, G. (1980), A feature-integration theory of attention, Cognitive Psychology 12(1); overview at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_integration_theory and the 40-years-later retrospective at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7039157/

sources.claim: WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast, Level AA) requires user interface components and their states to have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors; disabled/inactive components and purely decorative graphics are exempt
sources.source: W3C WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11, summarized at https://www.wcag.com/designers/1-4-11-non-text-contrast/ and https://dequeuniversity.com/resources/wcag2.1/1.4.11-non-text-contrast

sources.claim: The 60-30-10 color-allocation rule (60% dominant, 30% secondary, 10% accent) is a long-standing design convention with unclear origin and no located controlled study validating the specific ratios; it functions as a usable heuristic default, not a proven optimum
sources.source: General design-press coverage surveyed, e.g. https://planner5d.com/blog/60-30-10-rule-in-design/ and https://www.behr.com/colorfullybehr/tried-and-true-color-combinations/; no primary empirical study located in this search

verified.title: Blue-coverage percent + accent-hue count sweep

claim_verdicts.claim: Treisman and Gelade (1980) Feature Integration Theory: a singleton unique-color target pops out via fast pre-attentive parallel processing with reaction time flat against distractor count, contingent on the target staying rare/unique in the field; conjunction searches (two+ shared features) scale linearly with distractor count instead
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed against the primary paper (Cognitive Psychology 12, 97-136, 1980) and independent secondary sources (Wikipedia FIT overview, CUNY Sensation and Perception textbook). Flat-RT-for-singleton vs linear-RT-for-conjunction is textbook-standard and correctly stated. Minor nuance for residual_risks: FIT's strict pre-attentive/attentive dichotomy has been refined by later models (Wolfe's Guided Search); this does not undercut the specific pop-out-degrades-with-density mechanism the draft cites, so T1 stands, but the draft should not imply FIT is unrevised orthodoxy.

claim_verdicts.claim: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA) requires UI components and their states to hold 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors; disabled/inactive components and purely decorative graphics are exempt
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed via W3C-aligned secondary sources (Deque University, wcag.com, Knowbility, TestParty). Exemption list matches exactly: inactive/disabled components exempt, decorative graphics exempt, user-agent unmodified defaults exempt, logos/photography exempt. Draft's summary is accurate, not inflated.

claim_verdicts.claim: The 60-30-10 color-allocation rule is a long-standing design convention with no located controlled study validating the specific ratios
claim_verdicts.note: Correctly labeled CONV, not elevated to a research tier. This is an honest negative claim (no study found) rather than a positive empirical one, and the draft uses it only as an analogy to flag the existing LOCKFILE 3-blue-strings number as similarly unsourced, which is a fair and useful move, not a smuggled statistic.

claim_verdicts.claim: Solen's own existing squint-test ceiling of ~3 blue strings per viewport (0-1 on forms) is currently unsourced in the codebase, same evidentiary shape as a design convention
claim_verdicts.note: Verified directly against LOCKFILE.md lines 158-160 as quoted in solen_current; the line contains no citation or derivation, so CONV is the honest tier. This is the load-bearing self-critique of the whole stream and it checks out on inspection of the actual file text supplied.

claim_verdicts.claim: Proposed engineering thresholds (RGB<=10 / deltaE<=4 for blue-string match, 0.3% viewport-area hue-cluster floor, deltaE<=15 hue-token mapping, deltaE<=6 neutral exclusion, P_blue caps of 3%/1%, +/-20px staircase window, 4-5 co-occurring hues soft flag)
claim_verdicts.note: These are the research stage's own proposed engineering constants, not external empirical findings, and the draft already labels them as proposed/derived rather than measured, which is the correct honest framing. Nothing here is dressed up as a validated study.

verified.residual_risks: Two things for the owner, not blockers. First, this stream turns an existing soft, prose-only ceiling (~3 blue strings, LOCKFILE lines 158-160, itself unsourced/CONV) into hard pixel-level thresholds (RGB<=10, deltaE<=4/6/15, 0.3% area floor, +/-20px staircase window, 3%/1% pixel-coverage caps) that were never locked at that precision anywhere in LOCKFILE.md. These proposed constants are reasonable engineering defaults but are new decisions, not extractions of a frozen literal; per this task's own instruction they should not silently become enforced gates, they are a QUESTIONS.md / Taste Lab candidate for the owner to calibrate against real shipped screens (the draft's own taste_lab_probe section already proposes exactly this validation step against 8-10 approved surfaces). Second, Metric 2's 3%/1% P_blue cap is explicitly derived from Solen's own 80/17 CLAUDE.md rule, not from an external source; if the owner ever revisits the 80/17 split, this derived cap needs to move with it rather than staying pinned to today's numbers. No frozen LOCKFILE literal is being reopened by this addition itself.
